Rectitude

REK-tih-tood · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Rectitude is morally correct behavior/thinking.

Colleagues who disagreed with almost everything else about the old judge still trusted his basic rectitude.

Worked Example

The scholarship committee valued rectitude as much as raw talent, choosing the honest applicant over the more impressive but evasive one.

The committee is specifically weighing moral correctness -- honesty and doing the right thing -- against talent, which is exactly what rectitude names.

Your Turn

Answer correctly to continue.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

integrity: Integrity is the everyday word for a character whose actions match its values even when no one is watching. Rectitude means much the same uprightness, but it is formal and a little old-fashioned, and it measures conduct against a strict moral code rather than inner wholeness.

probity: Probity is uprightness that has been proven -- the tested, documented honesty of officials and their dealings, the kind that audits and long records confirm. Rectitude is broader and needs no ledger: it names strict moral correctness in a person's conduct and judgment of every kind.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

turpitude: wickedness or depravity

corruption: dishonest or fraudulent conduct

Where it sits · how unbending the moral standards are — honesty → rectitude → incorruptibility

honesty vs. rectitude: Honesty means simply not lying; rectitude describes a whole pattern of consistently correct moral judgment.

incorruptibility vs. rectitude: Incorruptibility pushes rectitude even further, emphasizing that no bribe or pressure could ever bend the person's judgment.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — rect

root — rect: straight, right (Latin (rectus))

suffix — -itude

suffix — -itude: state or quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: The root rect- ('straight, right,' from Latin rectus) plus -itude ('state of') gives 'the state of being straight/right' -- rectitude is the quality of always doing the morally right thing.

Use the root in a new word: correct

Use the root in a new word: correct: Correct shares the same rectus root as rectitude -- both are about being straight, accurate, or right.

Root Check

Word Choice

Rectitude is Turpitude's (this same unit) clean opposite: strict moral correctness versus deep moral wickedness. It has a formal, slightly old-fashioned register -- everyday speech more often reaches for 'integrity.'
